signals.title: Tool error not recovered: patch_file (README registration)
signals.description: patch_file was called 3 times to register the spec row in .moeb/README.md; all three invocations failed with 'error applying hunk #1. The diff context lines may not match the current file content'. Registration was completed via the Claude Code native Edit tool as a fallback. The 3 tool errors are recorded in RunState.tool_errors and caused the tool-errors rubric criterion to fail.
signals.proposed_resolution: Investigate patch_file context-line matching for extremely long lines (>300 chars). Consider using write_file with the full README content when patch_file fails, or improve patch_file's context-matching to handle long table rows. A targeted spec run to fix patch_file robustness on long lines would prevent this recurrence.

signals.title: patch_file context-line matching unreliable on long README table rows
signals.description: Table rows in the README spec index exceed 300 characters. Three patch_file calls using exact content from read_file all failed to apply, suggesting the context-line relocation algorithm does not handle very long lines reliably. This causes spec sessions that must add README rows to fall back to external tools, introducing a tool-error rubric failure.
signals.proposed_resolution: Add a moeb spec for patch_file robustness that implements a line-number-based insertion fallback: when context-line matching fails and the target line can be uniquely identified by substring, insert at the computed offset using line arithmetic rather than re-checking context.

summary: The spec was authored and registered successfully. The spec file satisfies all rubric criteria except tool-errors, which failed due to 3 patch_file invocations that could not apply context-line hunks to the README's long table rows. The README registration was completed via a native Edit tool fallback. The spec itself is complete, schema-compliant, drift-free, and well-formed. The persistent patch_file failure on long lines is a recurring reliability gap that warrants a targeted improvement spec.
